This process is modeled as a feedback loop where cognitive suggestion (S) influences motor neuron activity, leading to increased impedance (I_s) in targeted muscle groups. The resulting state of muscular impotence is not random but follows deterministic patterns based on the structure of antagonistic muscle pairs. Cataleptic equilibrium emerges as a long-term stable state within this system, characterized by minimal energy expenditure and sustained muscle tension. The physiological signature of this state—calm respiration, lack of tremor—is distinct from voluntary fatigue, indicating a fundamental shift in neuromuscular regulation. This suggests that hypnotic states are not merely psychological but involve measurable neurophysiological changes that can be mapped into formal dynamical systems.
